life_history: Steve is an adult male who identifies as health-conscious and is currently training for a marathon. He sought counseling to address symptoms of anxiety and insomnia. His target behavior is hazardous drinking; he consumes alcohol two to three times a week, often having three to four drinks at a time and sometimes bingeing with six or more drinks on weekends. Initially, he lacked problem recognition, believing his alcohol consumption was moderate and necessary for sleep, rather than recognizing it as a precipitant of his chronodisruption and anxiety.
intermediate_beliefs: Positive assumption: If I engage in drinking alcohol, then I can relax and fall asleep; negative assumption: If I stop drinking, then the anxiety and insomnia will overwhelm me and derail my marathon training.
intermediate_beliefs_during_depression: If I try to cut back on my drinking and still cannot sleep, it proves I have no control over my mind and body.
coping_strategies: Maladaptive coping includes self-medicating with alcohol to force sleep, as well as using minimization and defensiveness to protect his self-image from the stigma of hazardous drinking. Adaptive coping includes engaging in physical fitness (marathon training), attending counseling, and committing to a harm-reduction plan to decrease his drinking to no more than 18 drinks per week.

cognitive_models.situation: Lying in bed at night feeling restless and unable to sleep.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: On the nights when I do not drink, I have a harder time going to sleep. I need a drink to help me rest.
cognitive_models.behavior: Consuming excessive amounts of alcohol as a sleep aid.

cognitive_models.situation: Counselor suggests that alcohol is actually causing his anxiety and insomnia.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I do not really think I drink that much in the first place. I have a hard time believing that it is causing my anxiety. I am certainly not an alcoholic.
cognitive_models.behavior: Downplaying the severity of his drinking and defending his current habits.

cognitive_models.situation: Counselor shows a chart demonstrating his drinking falls into the high-risk, hazardous category.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: Jeez, no. I did not think I was that bad. I do not want to do anything to put myself at risk since I am a healthy guy.
cognitive_models.behavior: Acknowledging the risk, rating his readiness to change at a five, and proposing a concrete plan to cut back.
